findings.evidence: “Use the shortest supported path first; move maintainer and operator detail below it” and, at line 22, “Compare the actual output, file names, and flags with what the README shows” repeat model-known writing and validation practices. The Workflow section mixes expert checks with these reminders; Validation and References are largely activation, so expert material does not dominate the H2 sections by line count.
findings.fix: Condense the generic writing, delivery-format, and output-comparison reminders into one checkpoint. Preserve the concrete manifest fields, registry checks, release distinctions, generated-region rules, and renderer-specific traps.

findings.evidence: “a LICENSE plus a public remote or registry metadata means OSS” misclassifies a publicly hosted proprietary or source-available project as open source. Registry metadata can also belong to a private internal package, making this branch overlap the employer-hosted/Internal branch.
findings.fix: Before inferring OSS, check that the license actually grants open-source terms and that the intended audience is public. Treat proprietary/source-available licensing and private-registry publication as separate evidence; when audience remains consequential and unresolved, use the existing clarification fallback.

findings.evidence: “Load at most one guide per task” does not establish priority when creating or restructuring a README for Standard Readme compliance: line 40 selects section-checklist.md, while line 41 selects standard-readme-spec.md and then an example.
findings.fix: State an explicit routing order: Standard Readme requests load the specification instead of the section checklist, with the selected example allowed as a supplemental template; otherwise choose the single guide matching the task. Clarify that routine edits and audits load none.
